thread:
Marco: quick follow-up on the smokechain idea — sketched a lightweight flow we can iterate on. TL;DR: run tiny fast heuristics at intake, admit to bench only on 'uncertain' signals, fallback routing if bench backlog grows > threshold.

Anya: +1. can you paste the heuristics you used for 'uncertain'?

Marco: sure — rough rules: `if confidence_score >= 0.92 -> fast-accept`, `if confidence_score <= 0.55 -> fast-reject`, else -> bench. added a kv-cache-hit override: `if kv_cache_hit >= 0.85 -> fast-accept` to avoid bench for warmed prefixes.

David: curious about the bench backlog part — how do we decide to reroute? is it time-based or queue-depth?

Marco: proposed: both. two triggers. queue-depth > 120 and 95th p90 bench latency > 2x baseline => enable degraded-path routing to quantized-variant or lower tier. also ttl on rerouted items (max 2 retries to bench).

Sophie: what telemetry do we need to detect false-positives from heuristics? i.e. cases we fast-accepted but quality regresses.

Marco: good call. we emit an event for every fast-accept with these tags: model_id, prompt_hash, confidence_score, kv_cache_hit, route_version. downstream eval pipeline samples 1% and runs quick perplexity/LLR and a tiny prompt checklist. alert if sampled regression rate > 0.8%.

Anya: sampling 1% sounds fine initially. can we make the sample stratified by model family + token-length bucket? short prompts tend to be overconfident.

Marco: yes — stratify by `model_family` and `seqlen_bucket` (0-32,33-128,128+). Sophie: want to own the eval gating thresholds?

Sophie: I can. propose we start with these thresholds: perplexity delta > 1.5 or LLR shift > 0.25 triggers a regression alert. we iterate the numbers after 48h.

David: for failover topology, we need a safe fallback mapping from full-precision -> int8 quantized -> distilled variant. who owns the mapping table?

Anya: infra-team should own deployment topology, but ML should provide compatibility matrix (latency, perf delta). put mapping in model registry as `fallback_candidates` array.

Marco: agreed. registry fields: `fallback_candidates`, `compat_signals` (e.g. shape, vocab_hash, opset), and `quality_guardrails` pointers. scheduler can query registry when deciding reroute.

eng-ml-bot: note: added `smokechain-draft` tag to the RFC tracker and created issue #482 for telemetry hooks.

Sophie: one more operational thing — playbook for when reroute causes cascading load on quantized nodes. propose short-circuit: if quantized-util > 85% and bench backlog still high, shift new admits to degraded-mode: response with 202 + background-reprocess. need product signoff for UX.

Anya: product okayed background-reprocess for the edge case last month. we should surface the degraded-mode explicitly in Console with a per-model toggle and clear metric.

Marco: next steps: I'll open a lightweight PR with the intake adaptor changes and telemetry contract, Sophie will add gating thresholds to the eval-runbook, Anya will add `fallback_candidates` to the registry schema. keep thread for blockers. :thumbsup:

David: blockers: need a small bench-capacity simulation to validate thresholds before rollout. I can spin one up this week if we get the input format.

Marco: I'll attach the sampling input format in that PR — simple newline-delimited prompts + metadata JSON per line. thanks all.
